content.user_title: Build Reactive Go Pipelines with samber/ro
content.value_statement: Asynchronous Go pipelines can become difficult to compose, cancel, and test. This skill guides reliable samber/ro designs with typed operators and lifecycle controls.
actual_capabilities: Selects samber/ro operators for transforming, filtering, combining, and terminating streams.
Explains cold and hot observables, sharing behavior, and all five subject types.
Designs typed pipelines with Pipe functions and explicit error propagation.
Adds context cancellation, timeouts, retries, throttling, and bounded completion.
Recommends supported plugins for HTTP, scheduling, file events, encoding, and observability.
Identifies lifecycle mistakes that can cause missed events, silent errors, or goroutine leaks.
limitations: It does not replace current samber/ro API documentation or verify installed package versions.
It does not execute, benchmark, or test generated Go code automatically.
It is not intended for simple finite slice transformations better served by samber/lo.
Plugin examples may require adaptation for project-specific types, dependencies, and error policies.

use_cases.title: Design an event pipeline
use_cases.description: Choose operators, cancellation, and error handling for a service that processes asynchronous events.

use_cases.title: Review reactive architecture
use_cases.description: Assess hot and cold stream choices, subscription lifecycles, and resource cleanup before production deployment.

use_cases.title: Learn samber/ro patterns
use_cases.description: Translate channel-based workflows into typed observables while understanding subjects, composition, retries, and completion.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a samber/ro pipeline from [source]. Filter [condition], transform each value into [type], collect the results, and explain error handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a finite typed pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Add cancellation and retries
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a samber/ro pipeline for [operation]. Add context cancellation, a [duration] timeout, [count] bounded retries, and a final fallback.
prompt_templates.scenario: A service calls an unreliable asynchronous dependency.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a sharing strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare cold, Share, ShareReplay, Connectable, and subjects for [event source]. Recommend one based on [subscriber behavior] and lifecycle requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Multiple consumers need coordinated access to one source.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a production pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this samber/ro design: [description]. Find lifecycle, ordering, backpressure, concurrency, and error-propagation risks. Propose tests and a safer architecture.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs a production readiness review.

output_examples.input: Choose an operator for parsing JSON events while propagating parse failures.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use MapErr with a parsing function that returns a value and an error. Handle failures in the observer error callback.

output_examples.input: Five subscribers must connect before a shared source begins emitting.
output: Use a Connectable observable instead of Share.
Register every subscriber before starting the connection.
Define cancellation and completion behavior for the shared source.

output_examples.input: Review an infinite stream that has no timeout or unsubscribe path.
output_examples.output: Risk: the subscription can outlive its owner and retain resources. Add context cancellation, a terminating operator, and an explicit cleanup test.

best_practices: Handle next, error, and completion events explicitly for every production subscription.
Prefer typed Pipe functions and bound infinite streams with cancellation or terminating operators.
Use Tap operators for logging and metrics without changing stream values.
anti_patterns: Do not use untyped Pipe when a typed Pipe function can preserve compile-time checks.
Do not share a cold source unless subscribers require one coordinated execution.
Do not leave infinite subscriptions without context cancellation, timeout, or explicit unsubscribe behavior.

faq.question: When should I use samber/ro instead of channels?
faq.answer: Use samber/ro for composed asynchronous flows that need reusable operators, retries, timing, combination, or consistent lifecycle handling.

faq.question: When should I use samber/lo instead?
faq.answer: Use samber/lo for finite, synchronous slice transformations where stream lifecycle and asynchronous operators add unnecessary complexity.

faq.question: Does the skill generate complete Go programs?
faq.answer: It can propose focused implementations and architecture, but you must integrate imports, domain types, dependencies, and tests.

faq.question: Can it help prevent goroutine leaks?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends bounded streams, context propagation, terminating operators, and explicit subscription cleanup.

faq.question: Does it cover samber/ro plugins?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers documented plugin categories such as HTTP, cron, file events, encoding, logging, and rate limiting.

faq.question: Will every example match my installed version?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Confirm operator signatures and plugin paths against documentation for the version used by your project.
